mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased production costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Real Final Sales of Domestic Product (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which is a positive signal for corporate earnings and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) signals a slowdown in economic activity, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 7% and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1%, it signals a weak economy with accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates growing demand for housing and consumer confidence, which is a positive signal for economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is above 2%, it signals tightening monetary policy to combat inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates strong job growth, which is a positive signal for consumer spending and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite positive signal.
